newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court rules against punk group in police suit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court rules against punk group in police suit.

text.p: A federal judge on Friday awarded $2.2 million to a policeman and his union in a suit against a vulgarly-named punk rock group over its use of the officer's photograph on an album with anti-police lyrics.

Philadelphia Fraternal Order of Police attorney Michael Smerconish said the award was granted against the group "Crucif--ks," and its record company, Alternative Tentacles, run by former Dead Kennedys punk musician Jello Biafra.
The punk group was sued over its unauthorised use of a photograph orignally taken for a police-support rally. It showed Philadelphia policeman James Whalen pretending to lie dead beside his crusier.
The album contained songs advocating the killing of police officers.
"I'm hoping for every last dime these people have, up to the penny in their loafers if we can get it," police union head Richard Costello said in response to the verdict.
He said money would be used to provide scholarships for the children of slain officers.
After a court hearing on the case last week, Whalen said he had been shocked by the use of the photograph, and that he hoped it would send a message to record companies.
A person answering the telephone at Alternative Tentacles referred callers to the company's lawyer and said "there are motions pending." The lawyer did not return a call seeking comment.
